main_point: A Swedish court sentenced four administrators of The Pirate Bay to prison and damages for copyright infringement, but the site's operators claim the verdict is a media stunt and refuse to pay the fines while planning to appeal.

statements.text: A Swedish judge ordered four people running the file-sharing website The Pirate Bay to go to jail for a minimum of one year and to pay compensation. This decision proves that the site's operators are legally responsible for copyright violations, even though the site is still running.
statements.text_short: A Swedish court sentenced four The Pirate Bay administrators to prison and damages for copyright infringement.

statements.text: The Stockholm district court has determined that four specific individuals are legally responsible as accessories to copyright infringement, resulting in a formal conviction that mandates a one-year prison sentence for each defendant.
statements.text_short: The Stockholm district court found four people guilty of copyright infringement and gave them one-year prison sentences.

statements.text: The operators of The Pirate Bay characterize the Swedish court's verdict as a theatrical media stunt designed to generate headlines, asserting that the decision will not disrupt their file-sharing services or force them to pay the imposed damages while they prepare to appeal the ruling.
statements.text_short: The operators of The Pirate Bay dismissed the court's verdict as a media stunt and refuse to pay the fines.
